prose.text: **The order.** - Phase A: the formatter, the linter, the rig library cases, the `KR` rehearsals, the whole rehearsal binary (which   holds `HB` and every earlier arm under the unchanged `settle`), and the workspace unit layer. - The round: entries 7–20, `round` and `live` entries ONLY (`inputs#I6` item 6). Its after-reads of state other   actors move are keyed to the round. The whole-round dry-run is shown on the P5 card. - After the span: the census keyed `operator` and the report-only ledger read; then the whole integration layer and   the operator pass.

**What is not run, and why.** - No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10). - No `--e2e` layer: no MCP, contract or path surface is touched; the rig is test-only. - No release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it). - `cargo deny check` is CI's `supply-chain` job: no dependency is added. - No product file changes, so no smoke beyond the operator pass's harness boot. - No `KR` or `KR8` live entry: `KR`'s reading stands as taken (`inputs#I6` item 1) and `KR8` is spent; neither re-fires. - No 2.1.330 install probe: no 2.1.330 start runs in this round.

**Bounds.** Every test start runs under a test-owned home. Every waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint; the rehearsals wait on the rig's exit under its `--deadline`, unchanged. `KR8-2` runs under the rig's private scratch and config; `--deadline 300` bounds it under its entry's `timeout`. A key whose redraw never comes now waits the `--settle 10` bound (step 7), so a fully lost start can take up to ~26 × 10 s, inside the 300 s deadline. The non-priming probes of the live leg are the round entries ahead of it.

**The remove-the-guard controls** (validation check 4 (6); implement's one-shot `gate.py control`, never an entry; ids of 1–16 characters, each on a filtered entry, `inputs#I6` item 7). Both fire entry 3 (the rig library cases, filtered `test(/^rig::/)`, `--no-fail-fast`), `--timeout 1200`, a `timeout` reading NOT read as held: - `kr-after-key` — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`: the edit removes `settled_after`'s clause that the last drained   byte be later than the mark; case `rig::tests::a_byte_drained_before_the_key_never_settles_it`. - `kr-box-reread` — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`: the edit makes `kr_box_word` read a clean re-read as `dirty`   (its `late-redraw` arm removed); case `rig::tests::the_kr_box_word_tells_a_late_redraw_from_a_dirty_box`.
Implement writes the controls file with each edit's exact `old` text as its own code holds it, once steps 7–8 are written and entry 3 reads green.

**The live atoms' must-pass readings** (validation check 4 (9)). The `KR` summary keys the live entry asserts are this chunk's own print site, each read printed before any graded use, in block order: entry 3 (the pure words, `late-redraw` and the box words among them) and entry 4 (the rehearsals print `arm: kr`, `keys: x 13, del 13`, `control: told-apart`, `rounds: 12`, `late-redraw`, `dirty-box`, and the rig's teardown keys over the fake agent). `kr-reading` on a real CLI is the reading itself, asserted only by entries 19–20. Their must-pass and must-fail control is read at P5, typed over a synthetic ledger as at the take-up (`p5-controls.md` of this run).
